items.prose: The point on the unit circle is at 240°.
items.question: What is $\cos 240^\circ$?

options.why: You used $\cos 60^\circ$ and kept its sign. At 240° the point is left of the vertical axis.
That is $\sin 240^\circ$, the height. Cosine is the across-distance.
You took the height and dropped its sign. Cosine is the across-distance, and it is negative here.

feedback.correct: Half a unit left of the centre.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the across-distance, sign included.

explain.text: 240° is 60° past the half turn, so the point is the 60° point sent to the opposite side. The 60° point is $(0.5, 0.87)$. So the 240° point is $(-0.5, -0.87)$ and $\cos 240^\circ = -0.5$.

options.why: You turned $\tfrac{270}{180}$ upside down. 270° is more than a half turn, so it is more than $\pi$.
You divided by 360 instead of 180. $\pi$ radians is a half turn, 180°.
You multiplied by $\pi$ but did not divide by 180.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply by $\tfrac{\pi}{180}$ and simplify.

explain.text: 270° is three quarter turns, and each quarter turn is $\tfrac{\pi}{2}$. So 270° is $\tfrac{3\pi}{2}$ radians. The formula agrees: $\tfrac{270}{180}\pi = \tfrac{3}{2}\pi$.

items.prose: Sine repeats as the point goes round again.
items.question: Which expression equals $\sin x$ for every $x$?

options.why: A half turn sends the point to the opposite side, so $\sin(x + \pi) = -\sin x$.
Doubling the angle squeezes the wave. $\sin(2x)$ has period $\pi$, and differs from $\sin x$ at most angles.
Adding $2\pi$ outside lifts the wave by about 6.28. The full turn has to go inside, with the angle.

feedback.correct: A full turn returns the point to where it was.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Which change brings the point back to the same place?

explain.text: Adding $2\pi$ to the angle adds one full turn. The point ends where it started, so the height is the same. Hence $\sin(x + 2\pi) = \sin x$.

items.question: What is its period? Give two decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The period of $\sin(bx)$ is $\tfrac{2\pi}{b}$.

byKey.stretch: You multiplied $2\pi$ by 4. The 4 squeezes the wave, so divide.
byKey.keep: That is the period of $\sin x$. The 4 fits four waves into $2\pi$.
byKey.amp: You divided by 3, the amplitude. The period depends only on the number multiplying $x$.

explain.text: The angle $4x$ completes a turn when $x = \tfrac{2\pi}{4} = \tfrac{\pi}{2}$. The 3 sets the height and leaves the width alone. So the period is about 1.57.

items.prose: A point on the unit circle has $\cos\theta = 0.8$ and $\sin\theta = -0.6$.
items.question: Which quadrant is it in?

options.why: The first quadrant has both values positive. A negative sine puts the point below the axis.
In the second quadrant cosine is negative and sine positive. This point has the reverse.
In the third quadrant cosine is negative too. Here cosine is 0.8, so the point is right of centre.

feedback.correct: Right of centre, below the axis: the fourth quadrant.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Use each sign: cosine for left or right, sine for up or down.

explain.text: $\cos\theta = 0.8 > 0$ puts the point right of the vertical axis. $\sin\theta = -0.6 < 0$ puts it below the horizontal axis. Right and below is the fourth quadrant.

items.prose: A circle has radius 5 cm. An angle of 72° sits at its centre.
items.question: How long is the arc it cuts off, in cm? Give two decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Turn 72° into radians, then use $s = r\theta$.

byKey.degrees: You used $s = r\theta$ with $\theta$ in degrees. The rule needs radians: $72^\circ = \tfrac{2\pi}{5}$.
byKey.no-r: That is the angle in radians, the arc on a circle of radius 1. Multiply by the radius, 5.

explain.text: $72^\circ = 72 \times \tfrac{\pi}{180} = \tfrac{2\pi}{5}$ radians. Then $s = r\theta = 5 \times \tfrac{2\pi}{5} = 2\pi \approx 6.28$ cm. Check: 72° is a fifth of a turn, and a fifth of the circumference $10\pi$ is $2\pi$.

items.prose: Combine radians with the unit circle.
items.question: What is $\cos\tfrac{7\pi}{6}$? Give two decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Place the point first: $\tfrac{7\pi}{6}$ is just past a half turn.

byKey.no-sign: You found the size, but the point is left of the centre. Its across-distance is negative.
byKey.sin: That is $\sin\tfrac{7\pi}{6}$, the height. Cosine is the across-distance.

explain.text: $\tfrac{7\pi}{6} = \pi + \tfrac{\pi}{6}$, which is 210°: just past a half turn. The point is the $\tfrac{\pi}{6}$ point sent to the opposite side. So $\cos\tfrac{7\pi}{6} = -\cos\tfrac{\pi}{6} \approx -0.87$.

items.prose: A wave $y = a\sin(bx) + d$, with $a$ and $b$ positive, peaks at 7 and dips to 1. One full wave is 8 units wide.
items.question: Which values fit?

options.why: You took the peak-to-trough height, 6, as the amplitude. The amplitude is half of it.
You used the period as $b$. The period is $\tfrac{2\pi}{b}$, so $b = \tfrac{2\pi}{8}$.
You set the middle line at the trough. It sits halfway between 1 and 7.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the middle line first, then the amplitude, then $b$ from the period.

explain.text: The middle line is halfway: $d = \tfrac{7 + 1}{2} = 4$. The amplitude is the distance up to the peak: $a = 7 - 4 = 3$. A period of 8 needs $\tfrac{2\pi}{b} = 8$, so $b = \tfrac{\pi}{4}$.

items.prose: A trading volume pattern repeats every 5 days. We model it with $\sin(\omega t)$, $t$ in days.
items.question: What is the angular frequency $\omega$, in radians per day? Give four decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. One full cycle is $2\pi$ radians, shared over 5 days.

byKey.degrees: 72 is degrees per day. Models of cycles use radians: $2\pi$ per cycle.
byKey.turns: That is the fraction of a cycle per day. Multiply by $2\pi$ for radians.
byKey.times: You multiplied $2\pi$ by 5. The cycle shares $2\pi$ over 5 days, so divide.

explain.text: Over 5 days the angle $\omega t$ must run through one full turn, $2\pi$. So $5\omega = 2\pi$ and $\omega = \tfrac{2\pi}{5} \approx 1.2566$. The period is then $\tfrac{2\pi}{\omega} = 5$ days, as it must be.
